title: Microsoft Dataverse: semantic data understanding for agents and Copilot
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, preview behavior, billing qualifications and documented controls are supported. Minor corrections concern the omitted environment-selection step, differing Microsoft role guidance and checklist controls missing from the table.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The semantic model supplies shared business understanding for agents and Copilot rather than raw schema names alone.
claims.quote: The Dataverse semantic model gives AI agents and Copilot experiences a shared, business-aware understanding of your Dataverse data.

claims.claim: Dataverse extracts existing table relationships as semantic signals.
claims.quote: The semantic model automatically extracts signals from metadata that already exists in your Dataverse environment - table relationships, views, forms, column description summaries, and optionally sample data rows.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Public views and sub-grid views contribute semantic signals.
claims.quote: Public views with join conditions and sub-grid views that define which records and columns are relevant for a scenario.

claims.claim: Form display names contribute semantic signals.
claims.quote: For forms, only the display name is captured.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Descriptions of tables and columns contribute semantic understanding.
claims.quote: Description summaries | Descriptions added to tables and columns that explain what they represent.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: When enabled, sample rows contribute representative data values to semantic understanding.
claims.quote: Sample data rows | Representative rows showing what data looks like in each column.

claims.claim: Makers can view generated understanding per table in Power Apps and identify understanding gaps.
claims.quote: View generated semantic knowledge per entity — including name, description, and sample questions — directly in the Power Apps maker portal. Search for understanding gaps

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Makers can add glossary entries for domain-specific terms and acronyms.
claims.quote: The glossary allows makers to add domain-specific terms, acronyms, synonyms, and definitions that system signals can't infer.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The semantic model regenerates automatically every 12 hours.
claims.quote: The semantic model regenerates automatically every 12 hours to reflect schema changes.

claims.claim: Manual semantic model regeneration is available.
claims.quote: You can also trigger a manual regeneration at any time.

claims.claim: Initial generation can take up to two hours.
claims.quote: Initial generation can take up to two hours

claims.claim: Learn documents the semantic model and these controls as preview functionality subject to change.
claims.quote: This is a preview feature. ... Preview offerings are provided as-is and may be modified or discontinued at any time.

claims.claim: Automatic extraction of existing metadata reduces manual agent setup.
claims.quote: Reduced setup time — The model automatically extracts semantic knowledge from your existing Dataverse environment.

claims.claim: Agents sharing a semantic model share its understanding and can return consistent answers.
claims.quote: When multiple agents reference the same semantic model, they share the same understanding of your data and return consistent responses across experiences.

claims.claim: The platform automatically provisions the semantic model when Copilot experiences over Dataverse data are enabled.
claims.quote: The platform automatically provisions the semantic model when you enable Copilot experiences over Dataverse data, so you don't need to set up anything manually to start.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Sample data rows are disabled by default.
claims.quote: The sample data rows signal is disabled by default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout; summary; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Tables holding sensitive or regulated data can be excluded from a semantic model.
claims.quote: When a table contains sensitive, regulated, or irrelevant data, you can exclude it from the semantic model without disabling the entire signal type.

claims.claim: Learn does not describe a separate security-enforcement mechanism for the semantic model itself.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse semantic model security roles row column security; Dataverse semantic model security permissions sample metadata. Read overview, fine-tune, FAQ and Ask get-started: caller data permissions are documented, not separate model-content enforcement.

claims.claim: Computed semantic signals are read-only.
claims.quote: Computed signals are read-only. You can't directly edit an artifact generated by the system.

claims.claim: Glossary definitions can correct system-generated understanding.
claims.quote: To override system-generated understanding, use the Glossary to add a corrected definition.

claims.claim: Changes to a shared semantic model apply to all associated apps and agents.
claims.quote: If multiple apps or agents share the same semantic model ... changes to that model apply to all experiences associated with it.

claims.claim: A separate licensing model for semantic-model generation is not published, so the feature-specific licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse semantic model pricing license. Read semantic-model overview, fine-tune prerequisites, FAQ and Work IQ understand-costs; Ask licensing points to consuming Work IQ access. No separate generation licence is stated.

claims.claim: No separate charge for generating the semantic model is published at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse semantic model pricing license. Read semantic-model overview, fine-tune, FAQ, Work IQ understand-costs and Ask get-started; consumption and index storage are documented, but no separate generation price.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ costs follow the consuming experience rather than a dedicated business applications category.
claims.quote: For Business Applications in Work IQ, you track cost by the experiences people use rather than by a dedicated business applications category.

claims.claim: Copilot Chat's applicable entitlement includes business-data grounding in the licensed chat scenario.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat: The applicable entitlement includes business-data grounding in the licensed chat scenario. You don't pay extra for it as a Work IQ API interaction.

claims.claim: Microsoft directs readers to the consuming experience's billing guidance for other agents, including Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Other supported agents and services: To identify the applicable treatment, review the billing guidance for the consuming experience, including Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: Semantic modeling uses extra storage for search indexes.
claims.quote: Some features use extra storage for search indexes. These features include semantic modeling and access to Power Apps and Dynamics 365 data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Underlying application services may continue to incur licence fees during preview for consumption-based services.
claims.quote: For consumption-based services, usage of underlying application services may continue to incur license fees during the preview period.

claims.claim: The documented semantic model applies in environments where Dataverse intelligence is enabled.
claims.quote: Once Dataverse intelligence is enabled, the semantic model is provisioned automatically.

claims.claim: Learn names Dataverse MCP, Copilot in Power Apps, Microsoft Copilot, Sales Agent and Copilot Studio agents over Dataverse as semantic-model consumers.
claims.quote: a semantic model that powers agent experiences across Microsoft, including Dataverse MCP, Copilot in Power Apps, Microsoft Copilot, Sales Agent, and any agent built with Microsoft Copilot Studio over Dataverse data.

claims.claim: For the typical public production environment, the feature arrives on without administrator action, subject to the exceptions stated in Scope.
claims.quote: Starting in November 2026, Microsoft turns on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptions. ... The default applies to public production environments created for new or existing tenants.

claims.claim: Starting in November 2026, Microsoft turns on Work IQ for existing environments other than the listed exceptions.
claims.quote: Starting in November 2026, Microsoft turns on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptions.

claims.claim: EU and EFTA environments are exceptions to automatic enablement.
claims.quote: The following environments are exceptions: ... European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) environments

claims.claim: Government-related environments are exceptions to automatic enablement.
claims.quote: Government-related environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned by customers with current or previous government cloud deployments that are likely to depend on FedRAMP security controls.

claims.claim: Nonproduction exceptions include trial, sandbox and developer environments.
claims.quote: Nonproduction environments: This exception applies to trial, sandbox, and developer environments.

claims.claim: Signal settings, table controls and glossary changes apply only to the selected semantic model, not other models in the environment.
claims.quote: Changes you make to a semantic model, including signal settings, table-level controls, and glossary entries, only apply to that specific semantic model. They don't affect other semantic models in your environment.

claims.claim: Model names reflect their provisioning source, and the list shows associated apps or agents.
claims.quote: Name | The identifier of the semantic model. The name reflects the source that provisioned it. ... Associated apps or agents | Apps or agents that have access to this semantic model.

claims.claim: Table inclusion is managed in Power Apps through More > Semantic model > model > Configuration > table > Include in semantic model > Save and sync.
claims.quote: Sign in to Power Apps, and open the environment where Dataverse Intelligence is enabled. ... select Configuration ... Select the table, and then check or clear Include in semantic model. ... Select Save and sync.
claims.fix: Prepend the environment-selection step in controls[0].ui.path and its rendered table path: 'environment > More > Semantic model > model > Configuration > table > Include in semantic model > Save and sync'. The cited page requires opening the environment first.

claims.claim: Managing the semantic model requires System Administrator or both Semantic Model and Environment Maker.
claims.quote: You need either of the following security roles to manage the semantic model: System Administrator -or- Semantic Model and Environment Maker

claims.claim: If Semantic model is missing from More, makers can find it through Discover all.
claims.quote: In the left navigation pane, select More, and if not in the More list, select Discover all, and then select Semantic model.

claims.claim: No API equivalent is documented for toggling Include in semantic model on an existing model's table.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse semantic model API enable disable table signals glossary security roles row column security; Dataverse semantic model signals API. Read fine-tune and Ask manage-semantic-models: list/create/delete are documented, not changing existing-model table inclusion.

claims.claim: The environment Work IQ switch is in Power Platform admin center under Manage > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Work IQ.
claims.quote: select Manage. ... Select the environment that you want to manage. ... select Settings. ... Select Product > Features. ... Find Work IQ, and then turn the setting on or off.

claims.claim: The Work IQ environment-level setting requires an environment administrator account.
claims.quote: You need an environment administrator account.
claims.fix: Retain the cited role guidance, but append to the row note: 'Microsoft's participation guide instead lists Power Platform Administrator for managing settings.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/business-applications-work-iq/manage-participation, whose Before you begin section states 'Power Platform Administrator role to manage settings and assign other roles.'

claims.where: controls[1].governs, scope and note; Governance controls prose; summary
claims.claim: The environment Work IQ switch governs business skills, semantic modeling and Dataverse access through Copilot Chat, Research and Agent Builder, making them unavailable when off.
claims.quote: The Work IQ setting turns on business skills, semantic modeling, and access to Dataverse data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Research, and Agent Builder. If you turn off this setting, these features aren't available in the environment.

claims.claim: An API equivalent for the environment Work IQ switch is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Platform Work IQ environment setting API PowerShell enable disable semantic modeling; Work IQ setting API environment disable. Read default-settings, manage-participation excerpts and Ask get-started; these give UI setup, not an API for the switch.

claims.claim: Signal types, including Sample table rows, can be turned On or Off under How your data is understood and then saved.
claims.quote: From the semantic model overview page, in the How your data is understood area, turn a signal On or Off. ... Select Save.

claims.claim: Individual views and relationships can be turned On or Off under Configuration.
claims.quote: select Configuration, and search for the table display name ... Select Views or select Relationships to see the table's associated views and relationships. ... Find the item you want to exclude and turn it On or Off.

claims.where: Governance controls: No API is documented for any of it
claims.claim: No API is documented for the tuning operations and environment switch described in this paragraph.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse semantic model signals API; Dataverse semantic model API enable disable table signals glossary; Work IQ setting API environment disable. Read fine-tune, glossary excerpt, default-settings and Ask management: CRUD exists, but not these tuning operations.

claims.claim: Variable cost is appropriate because participating consuming experiences use the Copilot Credits meter.
claims.quote: Copilot credits are the unit used for the participating usage-based experiences. Prepaid capacity packs and pay-as-you-go billing through an Azure subscription provide ways to fund that consumption.

claims.where: Governance controls: not a separately documented generation-only toggle
claims.claim: A separate generation-only switch is not documented in addition to the broader Work IQ environment control.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Platform Work IQ environment setting API PowerShell enable disable semantic modeling. Read fine-tune, default-settings and manage-participation excerpts: environment generation control is described through Work IQ; no separate generation-only switch was found.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, At rollout and After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist's sample-row, glossary and disabled-signal controls are not all represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Keep sample data rows off'; 'Set a glossary owner'; 'Review glossary entries and disabled signals quarterly.' Table rows: 'Whether a table is included in a semantic model'; 'Work IQ features ... in the environment'.
claims.fix: Remove 'Keep sample data rows off unless there is a clear need', 'Set a glossary owner and a naming convention for terms' and 'Review glossary entries and disabled signals quarterly' from the checklist, leaving their explanatory coverage in the body. These checklist controls have no table row; do not add rows as part of this correction.
